James,

Brex's write-up on the Micronaut 4 upgrade says one engineer migrated 180 microservices in a month, and that the remainder still needs de-risking because some services had gaps in their test suites.

I'd start from the services still to migrate and the tests they lack, not from anything your team has already shipped.

Worth 20 minutes to compare notes?

drafts.name: Phil Burrows

email.subject: Agents off the laptops
email.body:
Phil,

The Micronaut 4 post was candid about what it took to run agents at Brex: the agentic loop broke whenever a laptop went to sleep, so the team provisioned dedicated nodes, configured headless authentication and moved to self-hosted Cursor agents.

The same post names what's left: the remainder of the migration, plus services where automated PRs passed existing tests and still caused runtime bugs. Devin runs in the cloud, keeps working when the laptop is closed, and tests end to end on its own VMs, so the next wave doesn't need more runtime upkeep from your team. Itaú used Devin to take test coverage from ~50% to ~90+%.

Open to 20 minutes on the remaining services?

drafts.linkedin_note: Phil, read the Micronaut 4 post on moving agents off laptops and onto dedicated nodes. I work on Devin, which runs in the cloud and keeps working when the laptop is closed. Would like to compare notes on the remaining services. Glad to connect.
drafts.linkedin_followup: Phil, one more from the migration post. The next step it describes is environment-aware agents that monitor staging and production for anomalies on migrated services. Devin can monitor incoming alerts, investigate them automatically, and come back with an investigation, next steps, and even a PR. At Modal, Devin produces a useful early investigation on 80% of incidents. It would sit alongside the pipeline your team already runs, not replace it. Happy to walk through how, for the next batch.
